newsitem.title: FRANCE: French beet sowings complete, planters await rain.
newsitem.headline: French beet sowings complete, planters await rain.

text.p: French beet farmers said on Tuesday they were worried that prolonged cold and dry conditions might cancel the benefits of early sowings.
Drillings were completed at the end of last week, ahead of last year, but a severe lack of rain and cold temperatures threaten to limit beet growth and harm yields, planters said.

"Sowings were completed in very good conditions but we now face two problems, a possible drought and cold temperatures that could cancel the advantages of early sowings," an analyst for the French sugar beet planters federation (CGB) told Reuters.
Beets across most growing areas are at risk since partial water restrictions are already in place in six departments of central France while fields in northern France are traditionally not irrigated.

France has had viturally no rain since January 25, the national meteorological service said last week, and farmers are increasingly concerned over the impact of a prolonged drought on grain and beet yields.
Environment Minister Corinne Lepage said earlier that unless it rains soon more regions may face water restictions.
France produced 4.23 million tonnes of beet sugar in 1996/97. --Dominique Vidalon, Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
